question: WAEC Results Statistics Summary A total of 1,959,668 candidates from 24,207 schools registered for the examination, while 1,950,726 candidates eventually sat for it. The main figures are: 1,200,514 candidates earned credits and above in at least five subjects, including English Language and Mathematics 1,687,378 candidates earned credits and above in at least five subjects, with or without English Language and Mathematics 1,834,695 candidates had their results fully processed and released 116,031 candidates still had results being processed 167,486 candidates had their results withheld Candidates can use the 2026 WAEC result checking guide to access their results. How Many Candidates Passed Five Subjects Including English and Mathematics? A total of 1,200,514 candidates, representing 61.54 per cent of those who sat for the examination, obtained credits and above in at least five subjects, including English Language and Mathematics. This figure was 1.42 percentage points lower than the result recorded during the 2025 examination. The five-credit requirement, including English Language and Mathematics, is one of the main figures used to assess candidate performance in the examination. How Many Candidates Earned Five Credits With or Without English and Mathematics? WAEC recorded 1,687,378 candidates, representing 86.50 per cent, who obtained credits and above in at least five subjects, with or without English Language and Mathematics. This figure includes candidates who earned the required number of credits but may not have obtained credits in both English Language and Mathematics. Male and Female Performance Breakdown Among the 1,200,514 candidates who earned credits and above in at least five subjects, including English Language and Mathematics: 558,883 candidates, representing 28.65 per cent, were male 641,631 candidates, representing 32.89 per cent, were female Female candidates recorded the higher number within this performance group. Overall participation figures also showed that 997,267 females, representing 51.12 per cent, sat for the examination, while 953,459 males, representing 48.88 per cent, participated. How Many WAEC Results Have Been Released? WAEC reported that 1,834,695 candidates, representing 94.05 per cent, had their results fully processed and released. The results of 116,031 candidates, representing 5.95 per cent, were still being processed when the announcement was made. Candidates whose results are still under processing may not see a complete result until WAEC finishes the remaining work. Why Did WAEC Withhold 167,486 Results? WAEC withheld the results of 167,486 candidates over alleged examination malpractice. The affected candidates represented 8.59 per cent of the total number who sat for the examination. Dr Dangut identified the growing use of mobile phones inside examination halls, despite the existing ban, as one of the reported concerns. Organised cheating in some schools was also listed among the infractions. The 8.59 per cent recorded in 2026 was lower than the 9.7 per cent withheld-result rate recorded in 2025. What Action Will Be Taken Against Examination Officials? Some supervisors and invigilators who were found assisting candidates with examination malpractice had been arrested. The affected officials would face disciplinary action through the relevant state ministries of education, according to the announcement. How to Apply for the Melajoom Foundation Scholarship Who Can Apply for the Melajoom Foundation Scholarship? The scholarship is for full-time undergraduate students who are currently enrolled in an accredited Nigerian university, polytechnic or college of education. Every applicant must also be an indigene of Owo Local Government Area and provide a valid Certificate of Local Government Origin. Owo Local Government Area Final-year students are eligible to apply. Students who already receive another scholarship or bursary may also submit an application, but they must disclose that support on the application form. How Much Is the Melajoom Foundation Scholarship? The award amount depends on the type of school attended by the applicant. University students: Up to N250,000 University students: Polytechnic students: Up to N125,000 Polytechnic students: College of Education students: Up to N125,000 College of Education students: These amounts are the maximum awards stated for the 2026 scholarship programme. What Are the Academic Requirements? The academic requirement depends on the applicant's current level of study. 100-Level Students Freshers at 100 level must have a minimum JAMB score of 250 . minimum JAMB score of 250 The JAMB score is the stated academic benchmark for this group. Students at 200 Level and Above Continuing students from 200 level upward must have a minimum CGPA of 3.5 . minimum CGPA of 3.5 Final-year students remain eligible provided they meet the applicable requirements. What Documents Are Required for the Scholarship? Every applicant must provide the general documents required by the Foundation. These are: Certificate of Local Government Origin Reference Letter from the Owo LGA Office, dated within the last 24 months Original Academic Goals Essay Other documents will depend on whether the applicant is a fresher or continuing student. Documents Required From Freshers 100-level applicants must provide: JAMB Admission Letter JAMB Result Slip The JAMB Result Slip should reflect the minimum score required for freshers. Documents Required From Continuing Students Applicants from 200 level upward must provide: Current Student ID Card Latest Academic Transcript Latest Academic Result Their academic record must also meet the stated minimum CGPA of 3.5. What Is the Scholarship Essay Question for 100-Level Applicants? A 100-level applicant must write an original Academic Goals Essay explaining the reason for choosing the course of study and how the degree will be used to make an impact in the applicant's community or field. The essay must be no more than 200 words . no more than 200 words Applicants should answer the stated question within that word limit. What Is the Essay Question for Students at 200 Level and Above? Applicants from 200 level upward must write about their most notable academic achievement or challenge and explain how they have maintained their academic performance. The maximum length is 300 words .

On the previous day, he had attended an all-night party – a late uncle's burial ceremony – where he had drunk himself almost senseless before crawling home in the early hours of the morning. Now, he got up shakily, splashed water on his face and hurried off to work, but not before carefully fastening on his upper left arm the amulet he had always worn for protection against accidents. A similar amulet hung concealed under the steering column of his bus. On his way, still feeling groggy, he caught his left toe against a stump and had some misgiving. It was a bad sign and he was supposed to go back home and then set out again. But there was no time for that now, so he hurried on. At the bus station, Dele quickly loaded his bus and sped off without any of the necessary checks on the vehicle. He had to make up for lost time. It was the rush hour, so the bus was overloaded as it often was, with many passengers hanging on to the doors. The tyres were threadbare, the brakes were faulty and the road was wet, but, still feeling a little sleepy, Dele sped on. Many passengers protested about his reckless driving, but he would not listen. After all, didn't he have protection against accident? As the vehicle took the last turn before its destination, Dele saw a broken-down truck blocking his side of the road. Under normal circumstances, he could have brought the bus safely to a halt, bur the circumstances were far from normal. The careering bus hit the parked vehicle, swerved wildly across the road and plunged into a ditch. Dele's surprise before he sank into oblivion was the failure of his supposedly protective amulets.

IBBU Direct Entry Screening Requirements Direct Entry candidates are required to upload their O'Level result together with a scanned copy of the applicable qualifying result. Accepted qualifications listed for the exercise are: IJMB NCE Diploma A'Level NABTEB is not acceptable for the Direct Entry screening. DE candidates will also submit the required result information during the online screening process. IBBU Post-UTME Screening Fee The prescribed screening fee is ₦2,000 . ₦2,000 Candidates will first complete an eligibility check, generate an invoice and then make payment through one of the methods stated on the screening portal. The available payment methods are Branch Collect or WebPAY, as directed by the portal. How to Apply for IBBU Post-UTME and Direct Entry Screening Candidates are to begin the screening process through the IBBU Post-UTME screening portal . The online process has three stages. Stage 1: Eligibility Check Candidates will enter their: JAMB Registration Number Phone number Email address An invoice will then be generated for payment of the ₦2,000 screening fee. Stage 2: Screening Fee Payment Candidates will pay through Branch Collect or WebPAY, based on the instructions displayed on the portal. Payment must be confirmed before the result submission stage can be completed. Stage 3: Result Submission After payment confirmation, candidates will log in and submit the required examination results. UTME candidates will provide their O'Level results, while Direct Entry candidates will also submit the required A'Level or qualifying result information. A maximum of two sittings is allowed. Candidates will also enter the appropriate scratch card PIN for each result type and provide any other required information. The acknowledgement slip should be printed after submission and kept for record purposes. New Scratch Cards Are Required for Result Verification Candidates are strongly advised to buy a new scratch card for each examination result being submitted. Each card should be used only once to check the result before its details are entered on the screening portal. The status of the scratch card matters because specified invalid card types will result in disqualification. Scratch Cards That Can Lead to Disqualification IBBU has identified four categories of cards that candidates should avoid. Invalid Card An invalid card is a card that does not exist or is forged or fake. Submitting this type of card will result in disqualification. Used Card A used card is one that has already been used to check another candidate's result. Candidates should obtain their own new card for the result being submitted. Exhausted Card An exhausted card has reached its usage limit. A card used up to five times is regarded as exhausted under the screening instructions. Expired Card An expired card is no longer active or valid. Candidates should check the card before submitting its PIN on the portal. Maximum of Two O'Level Results Candidates may present a maximum of two O'Level results during the screening exercise. Where more than one result is being submitted, the appropriate scratch card PIN should be provided for each result type as required by the portal. Awaiting Result Candidates Candidates whose O'Level results are not yet available may indicate Awaiting Result (AR) during the screening. Awaiting Result (AR) The outstanding result must be uploaded before the admission exercise closes. Candidates using awaiting results should therefore ensure that the required result is supplied within the admission period. False Information Will Lead to Disqualification Candidates are expected to provide correct information throughout the screening and verification exercise. Supplying false information will result in disqualification. The same consequence applies where any of the prohibited scratch card categories is submitted. Completion of Screening Is Required for Admission Consideration Every eligible candidate seeking admission through the 2026/2027 exercise must complete the online screening and verification process. Failure to complete it means the candidate will not be considered for admission. Candidates can check further University information through the official IBBU website .
